clue_checks.clue: My older brother was a tiller of the ground.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 4:2 says Eve 'again bare his brother Abel' after Cain, and that 'Cain was a tiller of the ground.' This clue could also fit Seth, but it is an early clue and the later clues single out Abel.

clue_checks.clue: I was a keeper of sheep.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 4:2 says 'Abel was a keeper of sheep.'

clue_checks.clue: The LORD had respect unto my offering from the firstlings of my flock.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 4:4 says Abel brought 'of the firstlings of his flock' and 'the LORD had respect unto Abel and to his offering.'

clue_checks.clue: My brother rose up against me in the field.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 4:8 says that 'when they were in the field,' Cain 'rose up against Abel his brother.'

clue_checks.clue: I was an Egyptian handmaid of Sarai.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 16:1 names Hagar as Sarai's Egyptian handmaid.

clue_checks.clue: I fled into the wilderness, and an angel found me by a fountain of water.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 16:6-7 says she fled from Sarai's face, and the angel of the LORD found her by a fountain of water in the wilderness.

clue_checks.clue: I called the LORD who spoke to me, Thou God seest me.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 16:13 matches the clue nearly verbatim.

clue_checks.clue: My son was Ishmael.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 16:15 says Hagar bare Abram a son named Ishmael.

clue_checks.clue: My eyes are described as tender.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 29:17 states 'Leah was tender eyed.'

clue_checks.clue: My father gave me to Jacob in place of my younger sister.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 29:23-26 shows Laban brought Leah to Jacob, who had served for Rachel. Laban justifies it by not giving 'the younger before the firstborn.'

clue_checks.clue: I was the mother of Reuben, Levi and Judah.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 29:32-35 records Leah bearing Reuben, Simeon, Levi and Judah. Omitting Simeon is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: My younger sister was Rachel.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 29:16 names Leah as the elder and Rachel as the younger daughter of Laban.

clue_checks.clue: My mother was an Egyptian handmaid.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 16:1 calls Hagar an Egyptian handmaid. The surrounding context of Genesis 16 shows she bore Ishmael.

clue_checks.clue: An angel told my mother my name before I was born.
clue_checks.reason: In Genesis 16:11, the angel of the LORD tells the pregnant Hagar to call her son Ishmael.

clue_checks.clue: My name was given because the LORD had heard my mother's affliction.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 16:11 says she should call him Ishmael "because the LORD hath heard thy affliction."

clue_checks.clue: My father was Abraham, but I was not the son of the promise.
clue_checks.reason: Galatians 4:22-23 says Abraham's son by the bondmaid was born after the flesh, while the son of the freewoman was by promise. The bondwoman's son is Ishmael.

clue_checks.clue: I was the youngest son of Jacob.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 42:4 names Benjamin as the son Jacob kept at home, and 42:13 says 'the youngest is this day with our father.' Together they identify Benjamin as the youngest.

clue_checks.clue: My mother died as I was born, and she called me Benoni.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 35:18 says Rachel named him Ben-oni as she was dying in childbirth, and his father called him Benjamin.

clue_checks.clue: Joseph's silver cup was found in my sack.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 44:12 says 'the cup was found in Benjamin's sack.' That the cup was silver and belonged to Joseph comes from Genesis 44:2, which is not shown. This is a minor added detail.

clue_checks.clue: My full brother was Joseph.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 35:24 lists Joseph and Benjamin as the sons of Rachel. Both are sons of Jacob, so they are full brothers.

clue_checks.clue: I was the brother of Rebekah.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 24:29 states Rebekah had a brother named Laban.

clue_checks.clue: My nephew served me seven years for my younger daughter.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 29:10 calls Laban Jacob's mother's brother, so Jacob is his nephew. Genesis 29:18 has Jacob offering seven years for 'Rachel thy younger daughter.'

clue_checks.clue: On the wedding night I gave him my older daughter instead.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 29:16 identifies Leah as the elder. Genesis 29:22-23 describes the marriage feast and Laban bringing Leah to Jacob in the evening.

clue_checks.clue: My daughters were Leah and Rachel.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 29:16 names Laban's two daughters as Leah and Rachel.

clue_checks.clue: I was the fourth son of Leah.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 29:32-35 lists Reuben, Simeon, Levi, then Judah as Leah's fourth son. This rules out the other three options.

clue_checks.clue: I said, let us sell our brother rather than kill him.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 37:26-27 has Judah asking what profit there is in slaying their brother and proposing to sell him to the Ishmeelites.

clue_checks.clue: In Egypt I offered to stay as a bondman in place of my youngest brother.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 44:33 has Judah asking to abide as a bondman instead of 'the lad'. The quoted verses do not themselves call Benjamin the youngest, though nearby verses (e.g., 44:23, 26) do. This is an acceptable paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: Jacob said the sceptre would not depart from me.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 49:10 says 'The sceptre shall not depart from Judah.'

clue_checks.clue: I was Jacob's firstborn son.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 35:23 explicitly calls Reuben 'Jacob's firstborn.'

clue_checks.clue: I found mandrakes in the field and brought them to my mother.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 30:14 says Reuben found mandrakes in the field and brought them to his mother Leah.

clue_checks.clue: I persuaded my brothers to cast Joseph into a pit instead of killing him.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 37:21-22 has Reuben say 'Let us not kill him... cast him into this pit.' 'Persuaded' is a fair paraphrase, and the brothers' compliance is confirmed in 37:24. Judah later urged selling Joseph, not casting him into the pit, so this clue points to Reuben.

clue_checks.clue: I planned to rescue Joseph and bring him back to our father.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 37:22 states his purpose was 'to deliver him to his father again.'

clue_checks.clue: My father was a priest of Midian.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 2:16 names the priest of Midian and his daughters, and Exodus 2:21 says 'the man' (that priest, per context) gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.

clue_checks.clue: I met my husband when he helped my sisters and me water our flock.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 2:17 says Moses helped the priest's daughters and watered their flock. Exodus 2:21 shows Zipporah was one of those daughters and became his wife.

clue_checks.clue: God sent my husband to bring Israel out of Egypt.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 3:10 is God's commission to Moses, Zipporah's husband per Exodus 2:21, to bring Israel out of Egypt. The shown verse does not name Moses, but the surrounding context (Exodus 3:4) makes the addressee clear.

clue_checks.clue: I circumcised my son with a sharp stone.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 4:25 explicitly states Zipporah took a sharp stone and cut off her son's foreskin.

clue_checks.clue: I was a Gileadite and a mighty man of valour.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 11:1 calls Jephthah 'the Gileadite' and 'a mighty man of valour.' Gideon is also called a mighty man of valour (Judges 6:12), but he was not a Gileadite.

clue_checks.clue: My brothers drove me out, and I lived in the land of Tob.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 11:2-3 says his father's wife's sons thrust him out and he dwelt in the land of Tob. They were half-brothers, called 'brethren' in v.3, so 'brothers' is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: I made a vow to the LORD before fighting the children of Ammon.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 11:30-31 records Jephthah's vow concerning victory over the children of Ammon.

clue_checks.clue: My daughter came out to meet me with timbrels and dances.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 11:34 states this directly.

clue_checks.clue: The LORD raised me up as a deliverer of Israel; I was a Benjamite.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 3:15 says the LORD raised up a deliverer, Ehud the son of Gera, a Benjamite. Othniel was also called a deliverer (3:9), but the Benjamite detail rules him out.

clue_checks.clue: I was left-handed.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 3:15 calls Ehud 'a man lefthanded'.

clue_checks.clue: I made a dagger with two edges, a cubit long.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 3:16 says Ehud made a dagger that had two edges, of a cubit length.

clue_checks.clue: I killed Eglon, the king of Moab.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 3:17 identifies Eglon as king of Moab. Verse 21 has Ehud thrust the dagger into his belly, and verse 25 shows him fallen down dead.

clue_checks.clue: The prophetess Deborah called me to fight.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 4:6 says Deborah sent for and called Barak and relayed the LORD's command to gather ten thousand men toward mount Tabor. Verse 4:4 names her a prophetess.

clue_checks.clue: I would not go to battle unless Deborah went with me.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 4:8: 'if thou wilt not go with me, then I will not go.'

clue_checks.clue: I led ten thousand men down from mount Tabor.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 4:14: 'So Barak went down from mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him.'

clue_checks.clue: I fought against Sisera, captain of Jabin's army.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 4:7 calls Sisera 'the captain of Jabin's army.' Judges 4:15 says the LORD discomfited Sisera's host before Barak.

clue_checks.clue: I took a Babylonish garment, silver and a wedge of gold from Jericho.
clue_checks.reason: Joshua 7:21 lists the garment, 200 shekels of silver and the wedge of gold, and Joshua 7:1 names Achan as the taker. However, neither cited verse mentions Jericho; they say only 'among the spoils' and 'the accursed thing'. The Jericho link comes from Joshua 6:17-19, which is not cited.

clue_checks.clue: I hid them in the earth in the middle of my tent.
clue_checks.reason: Joshua 7:21 says 'they are hid in the earth in the midst of my tent.'

clue_checks.clue: Because of my sin, Israel was defeated at Ai.
clue_checks.reason: Joshua 7:4-5 records the defeat at Ai, and 7:11 says Israel took of the accursed thing. The explicit causal statement is in 7:12, which is not cited, and 7:11 does not name Achan; his identity comes from 7:1.

clue_checks.clue: I was the son of Carmi, of the tribe of Judah.
clue_checks.reason: Joshua 7:1 says 'Achan, the son of Carmi... of the tribe of Judah.'

clue_checks.clue: My husband Elimelech and I moved to Moab during a famine.
clue_checks.reason: Ruth 1:1-2 says that during a famine Elimelech and his wife Naomi went to sojourn in Moab.

clue_checks.clue: My husband and both my sons died in Moab.
clue_checks.reason: Ruth 1:3-5 records the deaths of Elimelech, Mahlon and Chilion while the family dwelled in Moab. Naomi was left without husband and sons.

clue_checks.clue: I asked to be called Mara, because the Almighty had dealt very bitterly with me.
clue_checks.reason: Ruth 1:20 quotes Naomi saying this almost word for word.

clue_checks.clue: My daughter-in-law Ruth would not leave me.
clue_checks.reason: In Ruth 1:16 Ruth tells Naomi, her mother-in-law, 'Intreat me not to leave thee'.

clue_checks.clue: I was the son of Jonathan.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 4:4 states that Jonathan, Saul's son, had a son whose name was Mephibosheth.

clue_checks.clue: I became lame when my nurse fled with me and I fell.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 4:4 says his nurse took him up and fled, and as she made haste he fell and became lame.

clue_checks.clue: King David restored to me all the land of Saul.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 9:7 records David's promise ('will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father'), not the completed act. The fulfilment appears in 9:9 ('I have given unto thy master's son all that pertained to Saul'). This is a minor paraphrase, and the clue is still accurate in substance.

clue_checks.clue: I ate continually at the king's table.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 9:13 says he did eat continually at the king's table.

clue_checks.clue: I was the captain of King David's army.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 8:16 says Joab the son of Zeruiah 'was over the host' in David's administration.

clue_checks.clue: My mother was Zeruiah.
clue_checks.reason: The verse names Joab among the 'sons of Zeruiah'. That Zeruiah was a woman (David's sister) comes from 1 Chronicles 2:16, but the identification is standard and the clue is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: I killed Abner at the gate of Hebron.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 3:27: when Abner returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside 'in the gate' and smote him so that he died.

clue_checks.clue: I thrust three darts through Absalom's heart as he hung in an oak.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 18:14 describes the three darts thrust through Absalom's heart while he was alive in the oak. 'Hung' matches the immediate context (18:9–10) and is a minor paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I was a Hittite and one of David's mighty men.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 11:3 calls him 'Uriah the Hittite,' and 2 Samuel 23:8 with 23:39 lists 'Uriah the Hittite' among the mighty men whom David had.

clue_checks.clue: I would not go down to my house while the ark and the army stayed in tents.
clue_checks.reason: In 2 Samuel 11:11 Uriah says the ark, Israel and Judah abide in tents and Joab's men are encamped, so he will not go into his house. This is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I carried a letter to Joab that arranged my own death.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 11:14-15 says David sent the letter 'by the hand of Uriah,' ordering that he be set in the forefront so 'that he may be smitten, and die.'

clue_checks.clue: My wife was Bathsheba.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 11:3 identifies Bath-sheba as 'the wife of Uriah the Hittite.'

clue_checks.clue: I was the son of Solomon.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 11:43 states that Rehoboam his son reigned in Solomon's stead.

clue_checks.clue: I rejected the counsel of the old men and followed the young men.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 12:8 says he forsook the old men's counsel and consulted the young men. In context, 'he' is Rehoboam.

clue_checks.clue: I told the people, my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 12:14 matches the quote nearly verbatim.

clue_checks.clue: The ten tribes of Israel rebelled against me.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 11:31 gives ten tribes to Jeroboam, and 12:16 shows Israel departing from the king. Neither verse uses 'rebelled' or names Rehoboam directly; that wording comes from 12:19. Together they still support the clue in substance.

clue_checks.clue: I was a servant of Solomon, from the tribe of Ephraim.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 11:26 calls Jeroboam 'Solomon's servant' and 'an Ephrathite of Zereda'. Here 'Ephrathite' means Ephraimite, since Zereda was in Ephraim. But the KJV word does not say 'Ephraim' outright, and elsewhere (1 Sam 17:12) 'Ephrathite' means a Bethlehemite. The tribal detail therefore rests on interpretation rather than explicit wording.

clue_checks.clue: The prophet Ahijah tore a new garment into twelve pieces and gave me ten.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 11:29-31 states that Ahijah rent the new garment into twelve pieces and told Jeroboam to take ten, saying God would give him ten tribes.

clue_checks.clue: I became king over the ten northern tribes.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 12:20 says Israel made Jeroboam king over all Israel, with only Judah following David's house. Together with the promise of ten tribes in 11:31, this supports the clue; 'northern' is a minor paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I set up calves of gold in Beth-el and in Dan.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 12:28-29 states that he made two golden calves and set one in Beth-el and the other in Dan.

clue_checks.clue: A young prophet anointed me king over Israel.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 9:4-6 says the young man the prophet poured oil on Jehu's head and anointed him king over Israel.

clue_checks.clue: The watchman knew me because I drove furiously.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 9:20 says the watchman recognized the driving as that of Jehu the son of Nimshi, who drives furiously. This is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I had Jezebel thrown down from a window.
clue_checks.reason: In 2 Kings 9:30 Jezebel looks out at a window, and in 9:33 Jehu (the 'he' of the context) says 'Throw her down,' and they do.

clue_checks.clue: I destroyed the worship of Baal out of Israel.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 10:28 says 'Thus Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel.' Adding 'worship of' is a reasonable paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I was a king of the Chaldeans in Babylon.
clue_checks.reason: Daniel 5:30 calls Belshazzar 'the king of the Chaldeans' and 5:1 calls him king. However, neither quoted verse names Babylon. Babylon appears in the chapter (e.g., Daniel 5:7), so this is a minor addition. Nebuchadnezzar also fits this clue, but that is acceptable for an early clue.

clue_checks.clue: I drank wine from the golden vessels taken from the temple in Jerusalem.
clue_checks.reason: Daniel 5:3 says the golden vessels taken from the temple at Jerusalem were brought, and the king drank in them. Daniel 5:2 confirms it was wine.

clue_checks.clue: The fingers of a man's hand wrote on the wall of my palace.
clue_checks.reason: Daniel 5:5 says fingers of a man's hand wrote upon the plaister of the wall of the king's palace.

clue_checks.clue: I was slain that same night.
clue_checks.reason: Daniel 5:30: 'In that night was Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans slain.'

clue_checks.clue: I was the servant of the prophet Elisha.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 4:12 calls Gehazi 'his servant', meaning Elisha's servant.

clue_checks.clue: I told my master that the Shunammite woman had no child.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 4:14 has Gehazi answer, 'Verily she hath no child, and her husband is old.'

clue_checks.clue: I ran after Naaman and took silver and garments from him.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 5:20-23 shows Gehazi running after Naaman and asking for silver and changes of garments. Naaman bound two talents for him. The excerpt is truncated, but verse 23 completes the giving of the silver and garments.

clue_checks.clue: The leprosy of Naaman clung to me.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 5:27 says Naaman's leprosy shall cleave unto him, and he went out a leper. In context, Elisha is speaking to Gehazi.

clue_checks.clue: I was king of Persia.
clue_checks.reason: Ezra 1:1 explicitly names 'Cyrus king of Persia.' Darius and Artaxerxes were also Persian kings, but an early clue fitting other options is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: The LORD stirred up my spirit to make a proclamation.
clue_checks.reason: Ezra 1:1: 'the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, that he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom.'

clue_checks.clue: I declared that a house should be built for the LORD at Jerusalem.
clue_checks.reason: Ezra 1:2-3: 'he hath charged me to build him an house at Jerusalem... and build the house of the LORD God of Israel.'

clue_checks.clue: Isaiah calls me the LORD's anointed.
clue_checks.reason: Isaiah 45:1: 'Thus saith the LORD to his anointed, to Cyrus.' This clue uniquely identifies Cyrus among the options.

clue_checks.clue: I was king of Babylon.
clue_checks.reason: Daniel 1:1 calls Nebuchadnezzar 'king of Babylon.' Belshazzar was also king of Babylon (Daniel 5; 7:1), but this is an early clue, so overlap is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: I dreamed of a great image with a head of gold.
clue_checks.reason: Daniel 2:1 says Nebuchadnezzar dreamed dreams, and Daniel 2:31-32 describes a great image whose head was of fine gold.

clue_checks.clue: I set up a golden image and commanded everyone to worship it.
clue_checks.reason: Daniel 3:1-3 shows Nebuchadnezzar making and setting up the golden image. The command to fall down and worship (proclaimed to 'people, nations, and languages') is in verses 4-5, which the displayed excerpt cuts off with an ellipsis. The reference supports the clue, but the shown text does not include the command.

clue_checks.clue: I ate grass as oxen until I knew that the most High rules.
clue_checks.reason: Daniel 4:32 decrees he would eat grass as oxen 'until thou know that the most High ruleth,' and verse 33 records it fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar.

clue_checks.clue: My father was Zebedee.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 4:21 names 'James the son of Zebedee.'

clue_checks.clue: I was mending nets in a ship when Jesus called me.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 4:21 says James and John were 'in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them.' Peter and Andrew were casting a net (4:18), not mending nets, so this clue does not fit them.

clue_checks.clue: Jesus called my brother and me Boanerges, the sons of thunder.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 3:17 says Jesus surnamed James and John 'Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder.'

clue_checks.clue: King Herod killed me with the sword.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 12:1-2 says Herod the king 'killed James the brother of John with the sword.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a blind beggar sitting by the highway near Jericho.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 10:46 says blind Bartimaeus sat by the highway side begging as Jesus went out of Jericho.

clue_checks.clue: I cried out, Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 10:47 quotes this cry nearly verbatim.

clue_checks.clue: When many told me to be quiet, I cried all the more.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 10:48 says many charged him to hold his peace, but he cried the more a great deal. The clue is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I cast away my garment, came to Jesus and received my sight.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 10:50-52 describes him casting away his garment, coming to Jesus, and immediately receiving his sight.

clue_checks.clue: I was queen to King Ahasuerus.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 1:9 calls Vashti 'the queen' in the royal house of king Ahasuerus. Esther was also his queen, but this is an early clue, and the later clues rule her out.

clue_checks.clue: I made a feast for the women in the royal house.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 1:9 says exactly that Vashti the queen made a feast for the women in the royal house.

clue_checks.clue: I refused to come when the king sent his chamberlains for me.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 1:12 says Vashti refused to come at the king's commandment by his chamberlains.

clue_checks.clue: My royal estate was given to another who was better than I.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 1:19 proposes giving her royal estate to another better than she. Esther 2:17 confirms that Esther was made queen instead of Vashti.

clue_checks.clue: King Ahasuerus set me above all the princes.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 3:1 says Ahasuerus promoted Haman and 'set his seat above all the princes that were with him.'

clue_checks.clue: I was full of wrath because a Jew would not bow to me.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 3:5 says Haman was full of wrath when Mordecai bowed not. The verse itself does not call Mordecai a Jew, but that is stated in the surrounding text (3:4). This is minor paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: Pur, that is, the lot, was cast before me to choose a day to destroy the Jews.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 3:7 confirms that Pur was cast before Haman from day to day and month to month. The purpose of destroying the Jews is not stated in 3:7; it comes from 3:6 and 9:24. The clue therefore adds detail beyond the cited verse.

clue_checks.clue: I was hanged on the gallows I had prepared for another man.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 7:10 says they hanged Haman on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai.

clue_checks.clue: I was a ruler of the synagogue.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 5:22 names Jairus as one of the rulers of the synagogue. Nicodemus was a 'ruler of the Jews', not of a synagogue, so this clue does not fit him.

clue_checks.clue: I fell at Jesus' feet and begged him to come to my house.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 8:41 says he fell at Jesus' feet and besought him to come into his house.

clue_checks.clue: My little daughter lay at the point of death.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 5:23 quotes him: 'My little daughter lieth at the point of death.'

clue_checks.clue: Jesus took her by the hand and said, Talitha cumi.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 5:41 says he took the damsel by the hand and said 'Talitha cumi'. In context, the damsel is Jairus' daughter.

clue_checks.clue: I was a Jew who sat in the king's gate in Shushan.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 2:5 calls Mordecai 'a certain Jew' in Shushan the palace, and Esther 2:21 says he 'sat in the king's gate.'

clue_checks.clue: I reported a plot by two chamberlains to kill the king.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 2:21-22 names two chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, who 'sought to lay hand on the king.' Mordecai told Esther, and she certified the king in his name. 'Kill' is a reasonable reading of 'lay hand on,' but it is slightly more specific than the wording of the cited text. The minor paraphrase is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: I would not bow down to Haman.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 3:2 says 'Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence.'

clue_checks.clue: I raised my cousin Esther as my own daughter.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 2:7 says Esther was 'his uncle's daughter,' which makes her his cousin, and that Mordecai 'took for his own daughter.'

clue_checks.clue: I was passing by, coming out of the country.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 15:21 says Simon 'passed by, coming out of the country.'

clue_checks.clue: I was compelled to bear a cross.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 27:32 says 'him they compelled to bear his cross.'

clue_checks.clue: The cross I carried was the cross of Jesus.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 23:26 says 'they laid the cross' on Simon 'that he might bear it after Jesus.' In context it is Jesus' cross.

clue_checks.clue: I came from Cyrene and was the father of Alexander and Rufus.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 15:21 calls him 'a Cyrenian' and 'the father of Alexander and Rufus.'

clue_checks.clue: My sister was Martha and my brother was Lazarus.
clue_checks.reason: John 11:1-2 names Bethany as the town of Mary and her sister Martha, and says it was Mary 'whose brother Lazarus was sick.'

clue_checks.clue: I sat at Jesus' feet and heard his word.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 10:39 says Martha's sister Mary 'sat at Jesus' feet, and heard his word.'

clue_checks.clue: Jesus said I had chosen that good part.
clue_checks.reason: In Luke 10:42 Jesus says, 'Mary hath chosen that good part.'

clue_checks.clue: I anointed Jesus' feet with costly spikenard and wiped them with my hair.
clue_checks.reason: John 12:3 says Mary took ointment of spikenard, 'very costly,' anointed Jesus' feet and wiped them with her hair. John 12:1-2 sets this at Bethany with Martha and Lazarus present.

clue_checks.clue: I was an honourable counsellor who waited for the kingdom of God.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 15:43 calls Joseph of Arimathaea 'an honourable counsellor, which also waited for the kingdom of God.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a disciple of Jesus, but secretly, for fear of the Jews.
clue_checks.reason: John 19:38 says Joseph was 'a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews.'

clue_checks.clue: I went to Pilate and begged the body of Jesus.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 15:43 says he 'went in boldly unto Pilate, and craved the body of Jesus.' 'Begged' is a fair paraphrase and matches the KJV wording in Matthew 27:58.

clue_checks.clue: I laid Jesus in my own new tomb, hewn out in the rock.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 27:60 says he 'laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn out in the rock.' The surrounding verses (27:57-59) identify the subject as Joseph.

clue_checks.clue: I was a prisoner in Jerusalem.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 27:15-16 calls Barabbas a 'notable prisoner' at the feast. Jerusalem is implied by the context of Pilate and the Passover, but these verses do not name it.

clue_checks.clue: I had been bound with others who had made insurrection and committed murder.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 15:7 says Barabbas 'lay bound with them that had made insurrection with him, who had committed murder in the insurrection.' The clue is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: Pilate offered the crowd a choice between Jesus and me.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 27:17 gives Pilate's question: 'Barabbas, or Jesus which is called Christ?'

clue_checks.clue: The people asked for me to be released.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 15:11 says the chief priests moved the people to ask that Pilate 'should rather release Barabbas unto them.' This shows the people requesting his release.

clue_checks.clue: I was a disciple living in Damascus.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 9:10 calls Ananias 'a certain disciple at Damascus.'

clue_checks.clue: The Lord spoke to me in a vision about a man named Saul.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 9:10-11 says the Lord spoke to Ananias in a vision and sent him to enquire for 'one called Saul, of Tarsus.'

clue_checks.clue: I told the Lord I had heard how much evil Saul had done to the saints.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 9:13 says, 'I have heard by many of this man, how much evil he hath done to thy saints at Jerusalem.'

clue_checks.clue: I put my hands on Saul so that he might receive his sight.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 9:17 says Ananias was 'putting his hands on him' and was sent 'that thou mightest receive thy sight.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a king who came to Caesarea with Bernice to greet Festus.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 25:13 states that king Agrippa and Bernice came unto Caesarea to salute Festus.

clue_checks.clue: Festus told me about a prisoner named Paul.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 25:14 says Festus declared Paul's cause unto the king, describing a man left in bonds by Felix.

clue_checks.clue: Paul made his defence before me.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 26:1-2 shows Paul answering for himself before king Agrippa. Paul also defended himself before Felix and Festus, but this clue is revealed alongside others, so that is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: I said to Paul, Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.
clue_checks.reason: This is a direct quote of Acts 26:28, spoken by Agrippa.

clue_checks.clue: I followed Jesus from the baptism of John until he was taken up.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 1:21-23 requires the candidate to have companied with the apostles from the baptism of John until Jesus was taken up, and Matthias is one of the two appointed under that requirement.

clue_checks.clue: My name was put forward together with Joseph called Barsabas.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 1:23 names the two appointed: Joseph called Barsabas, surnamed Justus, and Matthias.

clue_checks.clue: The disciples prayed and gave forth their lots.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 1:24-26 says they prayed and gave forth their lots. The clue describes the event rather than Matthias directly, but it is accurate.

clue_checks.clue: I was numbered with the eleven apostles in the place of Judas.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 1:25-26 speaks of the apostleship 'from which Judas by transgression fell', then says the lot fell on Matthias and he was numbered with the eleven.

clue_checks.clue: I was a young man in Troas.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 20:6 places Paul's company at Troas, and Acts 20:9 calls Eutychus 'a certain young man' at that gathering.

clue_checks.clue: I sat in a window while Paul preached until midnight.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 20:7 says Paul 'continued his speech until midnight,' and Acts 20:9 says Eutychus 'sat in a window.'

clue_checks.clue: I fell into a deep sleep and fell down from the third loft.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 20:9 says he was 'fallen into a deep sleep' and 'fell down from the third loft.'

clue_checks.clue: Paul embraced me, and I was brought alive.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 20:10 says Paul 'fell on him, and embracing him,' and Acts 20:12 says 'they brought the young man alive.'

clue_checks.clue: Many gathered to pray at my mother Mary's house in Jerusalem.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 12:12 names the house of Mary, mother of John surnamed Mark, where many were gathered praying. Jerusalem is clear from the surrounding context of Peter's release.

clue_checks.clue: I went with Barnabas and Saul but left them in Pamphylia.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 12:25 says Barnabas and Saul took John Mark with them. Acts 13:13 says John departed from them at Perga in Pamphylia.

clue_checks.clue: Paul and Barnabas parted over whether to take me again.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 15:37-39 describes the sharp contention over taking Mark, after which Paul and Barnabas departed asunder.

clue_checks.clue: Paul later wrote that I was profitable to him for the ministry.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Timothy 4:11 has Paul write: 'Take Mark... for he is profitable to me for the ministry.'

clue_checks.clue: I departed from my master for a season.
clue_checks.reason: Philemon 1:15 says he 'departed for a season' from Philemon ('thou'). The word 'master' is not in this verse, but 1:16 ('not now as a servant') shows Philemon was his master, so this is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: Paul begat me while he was in bonds.
clue_checks.reason: Philemon 1:10: 'my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my bonds.'

clue_checks.clue: I was once unprofitable to my master, but now profitable.
clue_checks.reason: Philemon 1:11: 'in time past was to thee unprofitable, but now profitable to thee and to me.' 'Thee' is Philemon, his master.

clue_checks.clue: Paul sent me back to Philemon as a brother beloved.
clue_checks.reason: Philemon 1:12 says 'Whom I have sent again,' and 1:16 says 'Not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved.' The letter is addressed to Philemon (1:1).
